name: Anshu Chimala
role: Former Apple eng/design leadership · YC founder · AI design educator
bio: Anshu Chimala led software engineering and design teams at Apple for about 12 years, focusing on research and prototyping for future AI products. A YC founder, he posts AI design tutorials and demos on X and writes deeper craft notes on Substack. His guest essay in Lenny’s Newsletter (Sep 2026) maps an end-to-end process for tapping AI’s hidden creativity—loosely inspired by the Double Diamond, reimagined for a team of AI agents: Discover, Define, Deliver.

stages.title: Discover
stages.summary: Explore beyond average slop—vary directions and write bold, ambitious briefs before going deep.

stages.title: Define
stages.summary: Push past familiar patterns. Chain models, critics, images, and motion until the design has an individual identity.

stages.title: Deliver
stages.summary: Polish with restraint: cut clutter, kill AI tells, and rewrite the words that matter by hand.

highlights: Eight techniques · Discover → Define → Deliver for a team of agents.
Seed strings + ambitious briefs to escape SaaS-landing priors.
Critic subagents, image/video enrichment, then subtractive Deliver polish.
Primary source: Lenny’s Newsletter guest essay (Sep 2026); techniques 7–8 deeper detail paywalled.

name: Greg Huntoon
role: Manager, Designer Advocates · Figma · TC-EBC prompt framework
bio: Partial catalog from Greg Huntoon’s public Figma blog post “Cooking with constraints” and the TC-EBC reference repo. TC-EBC (Task, Context, Elements, Behavior, Constraints) structures prompts so LLM-driven design tools get clear intent instead of polite ambiguity. Earlier stub mistakenly listed David Kossnick here; authorship of TC-EBC is Greg’s. No endorsement.
highlights: Mise en place for prompts: clarity, context, constraints before heat hits the pan.
Polite fluff dilutes intention—models need clean instructions.
Revision discipline: put do-not-adjust rules in Constraints.
Five techniques catalogued (partial)—skeletons from the public post only.

stages.title: Discover
stages.summary: Task and Context lock what you’re building and for whom before Elements sprawl.

stages.title: Define
stages.summary: Elements and Behavior turn inventory + interaction into a buildable prompt.

stages.title: Deliver
stages.summary: Constraints hold the rails—especially what not to change on revision passes.

name: Nate Parrott
role: Product designer at Anthropic · built Claude Design
bio: Partial catalog from one public Claude blog post (no endorsement). Nate Parrott, a product designer at Anthropic who built Claude Design, describes using it to explore, iterate, and share visual ideas early—prototypes, decks, animations—before committing to build. This entry catalogs his published best practices and “make it alive” craft notes from that article only; it does not invent unpublished material.

links.label: Claude blog: exploring ideas before building

stages.title: Discover
stages.summary: Front-load intent, wireframe structure, sketch the indescribable, and generate many options to remix.

stages.title: Define
stages.summary: Specify look, bake brand into a design system, ground work in real product context, and make artifacts alive.

stages.title: Deliver
stages.summary: Point-and-talk edits, finish the last mile by hand, and keep collaborating without waiting on every turn.

highlights: Eleven practices from one public Claude Design post (partial).
Think before you prompt; specify look; system from assets; ten options then remix.
Sketch, point-and-talk, wireframe-first; last mile manual; real context; work alongside.
Make it alive — Bret Victor’s dead-fish warning as craft north star.

name: Adam Argyle
bio: Adam Argyle publishes design-engineering notes, CSS experiments, talks, and tools at nerdy.dev. Public materials identify him as a former Google Chrome/CSS advocate who continues teaching modern CSS and UI systems independently. Content spans defensive layout thinking and show-notes style craft posts.
highlights: nerdy.dev: CSS, UI, talks, and design-engineering notes.
Ex-Google CSS/UI education voice; still publishing publicly.
Emphasizes modern CSS as craft infrastructure.

name: Adam Wathan
role: Creator of Tailwind CSS · Refactoring UI
bio: Adam Wathan is the creator of Tailwind CSS and co-author of Refactoring UI with Steve Schoger. His personal site describes full-stack teaching through articles, talks, and courses, with Tailwind as the primary focus since working on it full-time beginning in 2019. Public materials teach practical UI design from a developer’s point of view.
highlights: Creator of Tailwind CSS; co-author of Refactoring UI.
Public teaching via adamwathan.me articles and courses.
Utility-first CSS as a craft tool for custom interfaces.

name: Ahmad Shadeed
role: UX designer & front-end engineer · Defensive CSS
bio: Ahmad Shadeed is a senior UX designer and front-end engineer bridging design and development. He coined Defensive CSS, wrote Debugging CSS, and publishes deep guides such as RTL Styling 101 on ishadeed.com. Public courses and lab experiments focus on layout systems that stay robust when AI output breaks.
highlights: Defensive CSS; Debugging CSS; RTL Styling 101.
Layout Maestro course for building layouts with confidence.
Public craft against brittle, AI-generated CSS.

name: Amelia Wattenberger
role: Principal research engineer · GitHub · novel UIs
bio: Amelia Wattenberger creates things on the web spanning data visualization, novel interfaces, and AI tooling. Public site wattenberger.com lists Principal Research Engineer work on a small R&D team within GitHub exploring novel UIs and ML. Earlier writing includes interactive D3 and React teaching materials.
highlights: GitHub R&D: novel UIs + ML; public research writing.
Known for interactive D3/React education essays.
Explores alternatives to chatbot-only AI interfaces.

name: Andy Matuschak
role: Applied researcher · tools that expand thought
bio: Andy Matuschak is an applied researcher focused on user interfaces that expand what people can think and do. Public work includes Quantum Country and an augmented book that helps people understand and remember what they read. Previously helped build iOS at Apple and led R&D at Khan Academy.
highlights: Quantum Country and memory-augmenting reading interfaces.
Prior Apple iOS and Khan Academy R&D leadership.
Public research ethos: more wonder, insight, and expression.

name: Brad Frost
bio: Brad Frost is a designer and consultant known for Atomic Design and long-form public writing at bradfrost.com. Work focuses on design systems, pattern libraries, and collaborative front-end craft between designers and engineers. Speaks widely on scaling interface quality without chaos.
highlights: Author of Atomic Design; design-systems consultant.
Public writing on pattern libraries and collaborative craft.
Advocate for systematic interface quality.

name: Bret Victor
bio: Bret Victor publishes at worrydream.com. He led the team that founded Dynamicland and invented Realtalk, a self-hosted spatial computing system. Previously at Apple he designed early iPad UI concepts and helped establish future-interfaces prototyping. Public talks include Inventing on Principle and Stop Drawing Dead Fish—widely cited against lifeless interface demos.
highlights: Dynamicland / Realtalk; prior Apple future-interfaces work.
Public talks: Inventing on Principle; Stop Drawing Dead Fish.
Essays: Ladder of Abstraction; Learnable Programming.

name: Brian Lovin
bio: Brian Lovin is a software designer in San Francisco currently making AI products at Notion. He co-founded Campsite, designed GitHub Mobile after Spectrum’s acquisition, and earlier designed payments at Facebook and was first product designer at Buffer. He co-hosted Design Details for years and created Staff Design, an interview project on IC career paths.
highlights: Designing AI products at Notion; prior Campsite, GitHub Mobile, Spectrum.
Created Staff Design and long-running Design Details podcast co-host.
Public site briOS collects writing, app dissections, and curated sites.

name: Cap Watkins
bio: Cap Watkins is Platform Design Director for QuickBooks at Intuit. Public bio lists prior Head of Product Design at Lattice, CXO at Primary, VP of Design at BuzzFeed, and design roles at Etsy and Amazon. His site notes human-written content and a focus on design leadership craft.
highlights: QuickBooks Platform Design Director; prior Lattice and BuzzFeed.
Public writing on design systems and designer-engineer craft.
Site explicitly human-authored—anti-slop posture.

name: Cassie Evans
bio: Cassie Evans works on GSAP (GreenSock) as a Staff Developer Relations Engineer & Product Manager under Webflow’s umbrella in public listings. She is known for teaching SVG and UI interaction craft—often described as GSAP’s “fairy codemother.” Public workshops and demos emphasize expressive motion with technical clarity.
highlights: GSAP educator focused on SVG and UI interactions.
Public workshops and demos for expressive, precise motion.
Staff DevRel/PM role listed publicly via Webflow/GSAP.

name: Craig Mod
bio: Craig Mod is a writer and photographer based in Japan whose public work explores walking, books, and careful digital publishing. Books include Kissa by Kissa and Things Become Other Things; essays appear on craigmod.com and in outlets such as The New York Times and The Atlantic. Practice emphasizes lightness, attention, and physical/digital book craft.
highlights: Books and essays on walking Japan and publishing craft.
Special Projects / hand-bound editions as anti-slop making.
Public rules: elevate everyone you encounter; quality of care.

name: Dan Mall
bio: Dan Mall is a design educator and systems practitioner publishing at danmall.com / Dan Mall Teaches. Public work covers design systems, product design leadership, and teaching designers to ship better organizational craft. Long-running independent practice with courses and writing.
highlights: Dan Mall Teaches: systems and product design education.
Public emphasis on design systems that teams can actually run.
Independent practice spanning consulting and courses.

name: David Hoang
role: VP of Design · Atlassian · Rovo & AI
bio: David Hoang is VP of Design for Rovo & AI (and related ecosystem work) at Atlassian. Public bio lists prior design leadership at Replit and Webflow and Head of Product Design at One Medical. He publishes Proof of Concept, a newsletter on design leadership, building, and experiments.
highlights: Leads design for Atlassian Rovo & AI initiatives.
Alum: Replit, Webflow, One Medical design leadership.
Proof of Concept newsletter for design GMs.

name: Don Norman
role: Cognitive scientist · The Design of Everyday Things
bio: Don Norman is a cognitive scientist and design researcher best known for The Design of Everyday Things. He co-founded the Nielsen Norman Group, helped establish UC San Diego’s Design Lab, and publishes at jnd.org on humanity-centered design. Public work underpins modern usability and affordance vocabulary.
highlights: Author of The Design of Everyday Things.
Nielsen Norman Group co-founder; UCSD Design Lab.
Public advocacy for humanity-centered design.

name: Emil Kowalski
bio: Emil Kowalski is a design engineer on Linear’s web team, previously on Vercel’s design team. He created Sonner (toast) and Vaul (drawer) for React, and teaches web animation theory and implementation through animations.dev. His public writing covers taste, friction, and when not to animate.
highlights: Design engineer at Linear; previously Vercel design team.
Creator of Sonner and Vaul; course at animations.dev.
Public essays on taste, judgement, and practical animation tips.

name: Erika Hall
bio: Erika Hall is co-founder of Mule Design Studio and author of Just Enough Research. Public work argues for grounded research, clear writing, and skepticism toward empty process theater. She writes and speaks on making digital products that respect users’ time and intelligence.
highlights: Author of Just Enough Research; Mule Design co-founder.
Public critique of empty UX theater and research theater.
Craft stance: clear writing and evidence over slides.

name: Frank Chimero
role: Designer · writer · The Shape of Design
bio: Frank Chimero is a New York–based designer with a long public practice across brand, product, and creative direction. He co-founded Abstract and wrote, illustrated, and published The Shape of Design (2012). Essays and lectures are widely assigned in design classrooms; current studio work is listed on frankchimero.com and studiofrank.co.
highlights: Author of The Shape of Design; co-founder of Abstract.
Public essays treated as foundational web-design texts.
Studio practice spans brand and product direction.

name: Imran Chaudhri
role: Designer · Apple alum · Humane / HP IQ
bio: Imran Chaudhri is a designer and inventor with a long Apple Human Interface tenure (Mac, iPod, iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and more). He co-founded Humane (AI Pin), later acquired in part by HP; public profiles list SVP Design & Innovation at HP IQ. Directory entry reflects published interface history only.
highlights: Long Apple HI career spanning major product launches.
Co-founder of Humane; later HP IQ design leadership (public).
Public storytelling on Watch and iPhone interaction history.

name: Jakub Antalik
bio: Jakub Antalik is a product designer and engineer focused on motion and craft. He previously worked at Frame.io (acquired by Adobe), Intercom, and as a Design Lead at 0x.org. He publishes transitions.dev, a free collection of essential UI transitions for web apps that can be copied as CSS/React or used as coding-agent skills. This catalog’s motion lab adapts free recipes from that project; Pro recipes were not used.
highlights: Author of free transitions.dev UI motion recipes used by this site’s motion lab.
Prior craft roles at Frame.io, Intercom, and 0x.org.
Public personal site lists motion components and agent-ready skills.

name: Jason Yuan
bio: Jason Yuan designs interfaces—the metaphors that humanize them and the systems that scale them. Public portfolio covers MercuryOS prototypes, kinetic type for Klim Type Foundry, and work at Apple’s Marcom UX and Human Interface teams. He studied theatre at Northwestern and graphic design at RISD; recent public work includes MakeSpace and Hivemind.
highlights: Public MercuryOS and Apple Marcom/HIG craft history.
Portfolio spans kinetic type, OS metaphors, and social software.
Emphasizes taste as distillation of many public no’s.

name: Jessica Hische
bio: Jessica Hische is a lettering artist and New York Times best-selling author based in Oakland. Public site jessicahische.is documents client lettering, books, and the well-known Should I Work for Free flowchart. Practice centers on typographic craft and thoughtful freelance boundaries.
highlights: Lettering artist with widely taught freelance craft resources.
NYT best-selling author; Oakland-based practice.
Public teaching of typographic taste and client craft.

name: Jonnie Hallman
bio: Jonnie Hallman (@destroytoday) is an independent design engineer in Brooklyn/New York, formerly at Stripe. His site destroytoday.com showcases landing pages and microsites as a craft focus and publishes process writing. Public GitHub and site document years of indie design-engineering work.
highlights: Indie design engineer; ex-Stripe; Brooklyn practice.
Public focus on polished landing pages and microsites.
Process writing at destroytoday.com.

name: Josh W. Comeau
bio: Josh W. Comeau runs joshwcomeau.com, an interactive teaching site for CSS, animation, SVG, and layout. He previously held senior engineering roles at Gatsby, DigitalOcean, and Khan Academy and now focuses on indie developer education. Public tutorials emphasize feel, performance nuance, and principles like squash-and-stretch applied to UI.
highlights: Interactive CSS/animation education without slop demos.
Prior Gatsby, DigitalOcean, Khan Academy engineering.
Open-source: use-sound, react-flip-move.

name: Julie Zhuo
role: Founder · Sundial · The Making of a Manager
bio: Julie Zhuo is founder of Sundial, author of The Making of a Manager, and essayist at The Looking Glass. Public site lists writing and talks on product leadership, career craft, and how product development is changing. She posts as @joulee.
highlights: Author of The Making of a Manager; founder of Sundial.
The Looking Glass essays on product and leadership craft.
Public voice for intentional management and product taste.

name: Karri Saarinen
bio: Karri Saarinen is co-founder and CEO of Linear. He was Principal Designer and design-systems lead at Airbnb, created founding design at Coinbase, and co-founded YC-backed Kippt and Rails Girls. Public interviews emphasize craft and focus in product building. From Finland; lives in California.
highlights: Co-founder/CEO of Linear; craft-first product ethos.
Prior Airbnb design systems and Coinbase founding design.
Public site lists Linear, Kippt, and Rails Girls history.

name: Katie Dill
bio: Katie Dill is Head of Design at Stripe. Public career notes include prior VP of Design at Lyft and design leadership at Airbnb, plus earlier frog design work. Profiles describe building high-performing design teams and sweating product details at scale.
highlights: Head of Design at Stripe; prior Lyft VP Design and Airbnb.
Public reputation for team-building and detail craft at scale.
Directory listing from public career sources only.

name: Kenya Hara
bio: Kenya Hara is a Japanese graphic designer and art director long associated with MUJI’s visual identity and the design firm Nippon Design Center. Public books such as Designing Design and White articulate emptiness, information design, and restraint as craft. Cited worldwide as a counterweight to visual noise.
highlights: MUJI art direction; Nippon Design Center practice.
Books: Designing Design; White—restraint as method.
Public philosophy: emptiness against visual slop.

name: Khoi Vinh
bio: Khoi Vinh is a designer and long-time design blogger at subtraction.com. Public profiles have associated him with Adobe design work and the Wireframe podcast. Career history includes prominent digital design leadership and continued writing on product and editorial design craft.
highlights: Long-running subtraction.com design writing.
Public design leadership and Wireframe podcast hosting.
Cited for editorial and product design clarity.

name: Linda Dong
bio: Linda Dong is a Design Evangelist at Apple. Public materials credit her with Apple Design Resources (including Figma/Sketch kits) and talks on principles of great design alongside Apple Developer Relations. Earlier Apple work included conceptual UI on a small prototyping team spanning iOS, Mac, and Apple TV.
highlights: Apple Design Evangelist; ships public design kits and HIG principles talks.
Prior Apple prototyping work across platforms.
Public posts announce design resources for developers.

name: Linus Lee
bio: Linus Lee publishes as thesephist.com, documenting research and advising on AI interpretability interfaces. Public bio lists prior Research Engineer work at Notion, Researcher in Residence at Betaworks, and earlier roles at Replit and related labs. Most active publicly as @thesephist on X and GitHub.
highlights: Public tools-for-thought and AI interface research writing.
Prior Notion, Betaworks, Replit research/engineering roles.
Active as @thesephist across X and GitHub.

name: Luke Wroblewski
bio: Luke Wroblewski (LukeW) is a digital product leader and author of Mobile First, Web Form Design, and Site-Seeing. Public career includes Google product leadership after Polar’s acquisition, earlier Yahoo and eBay design roles, and ongoing writing at lukew.com. Known for pragmatic mobile and form design craft.
highlights: Author of Mobile First and Web Form Design.
Public lukew.com essays on product and input craft.
Career spanning Google, Polar, Yahoo, eBay design/product.

name: Maggie Appleton
role: Designer · digital garden · tools for thought
bio: Maggie Appleton maintains maggieappleton.com as a digital garden of essays and notes on design, anthropomorphism, and tools for thought. Public work includes design engineering and illustrated essays that treat interfaces as cultural artifacts. She is often cited for making complex product and AI ideas visually legible without buzzword gloss.
highlights: Digital garden of essays on design and tools for thought.
Illustrated explanations of product and AI concepts.
Public craft voice for anti-slop clarity in interface writing.

name: Maxime Heckel
bio: Maxime Heckel is a New York–based frontend engineer whose public site and blog cover web development, shaders, and real-time 3D. Writing aims to document the articles he wished he had while learning visual craft on the web. Portfolio emphasizes well-designed, fast, delightful experiences refined against evolving taste.
highlights: Public teaching on shaders and real-time 3D for the web.
Craft blog aimed at builders leveling visual engineering taste.
Portfolio of fast, designed frontend experiences.

name: Meng To
bio: Meng To is a designer and teacher in Singapore who founded Design+Code, teaching designers to code and developers to design. Public materials describe tens of thousands of paid customers and courses spanning design and implementation. His personal site also documents sketchbook work and AI-era education experiments around DesignCode.
highlights: Founder of Design+Code education platform.
Public stance: craft education stays relevant amid AI slop.
Personal site pairs product teaching with observational drawing.

name: Naz Hamid
bio: Naz Hamid is a San Francisco–based designer, photographer, and writer. He founded the design studio Weightshift (clients spanning Abstract, Dropbox, Intercom, and others), helped build design at VSCO, and co-founded Aphera, a Mac photo editor. Public essays on nazhamid.com argue for human craft against AI particle-board aesthetics.
highlights: Founder of Weightshift; co-founder of Aphera.
Prior VSCO design leadership and long client craft practice.
Public essays: Craft Is Not Culture, Real Wood, The Drawing Hand.

name: Noah Levin
bio: Noah Levin is VP of Product Design at Figma. Public writing covers how Figma built its design team, career levels, and design process. Personal site and CV document a product-design career focused on tools that help people make better things.
highlights: VP of Product Design at Figma.
Public essays on Figma design process and career levels.
Focus on tools and teams for better making.

name: Pablo Stanley
bio: Pablo Stanley designs at Vercel on v0 after co-founding Lummi (acquired by Udemy) and Blush. Public career includes InVision design advocacy and co-founding design at Carbon Health. He is widely known for open illustration libraries such as Avataaars, Humaaans, Open Peeps, and Open Doodles.
highlights: Design at Vercel v0; prior Lummi and Blush co-founder.
Open illustration systems used across products.
Teaches UI craft publicly via courses and Substack.

name: Paco Coursey
bio: Paco Coursey crafts interfaces at Linear (webmaster) and previously developed Vercel’s design system, website, and dashboard. His site paco.me documents polished UI details, projects like a composable command menu (⌘K), and writing on React hooks and dark mode. Public profile emphasizes typography, motion, and performance as craft.
highlights: Crafting interfaces at Linear; prior Vercel design system work.
Public projects include ⌘K and Writer (plain-text editor).
Site focuses on magical UI details without hype.

name: Rasmus Andersson
bio: Rasmus Andersson is a Swedish designer and engineer in San Francisco publishing at rsms.me. Public work includes the Inter typeface and past roles spanning Figma, Facebook, and early Spotify. He frames software as a medium for expression across fonts, tools, and small art projects.
highlights: Creator of Inter; public design-engineering practice.
Past Figma, Facebook, founding-era Spotify craft.
rsms.me documents fonts, tools, and software-as-medium.

name: Rauno Freiberg
role: Staff design engineer · Vercel · interaction craft
bio: Rauno Freiberg is an Estonian interaction designer and Staff Design Engineer at Vercel. His public site rauno.me collects craft notes, Field Notes, and projects including Devouring Details and work toward a History of Software Design exhibit. He writes about invisible details of interaction design and the discipline of making interfaces fast, consistent, and carefully finished.
highlights: Staff Design Engineer at Vercel; public craft site at rauno.me.
Known for detail-obsessed interaction writing (e.g. Invisible Details of Interaction Design).
Projects include Field Notes and History of Software Design.

name: Robin Rendle
bio: Robin Rendle is a designer currently at Apple per public LinkedIn. He maintains robinrendle.com and is known in the web community for writing on design systems, typography, and the culture of making websites carefully. Directory entry uses public career and site presence only.
highlights: Public writing on design systems and web craft.
Personal site and GitHub document ongoing practice.
Listed as Apple designer from public LinkedIn only.

name: Ryan Singer
bio: Ryan Singer is known for product design and process work at 37signals/Basecamp and for Shape Up, the public methodology for shaping work before building. His site feltpresence.com collects writing on product craft; historically active as @rjs. Directory entry reflects published process craft, not affiliation.
highlights: Shape Up methodology; long Basecamp/37signals product craft.
feltpresence.com writing on shaping and shipping.
Public teaching of appetite-bound product design.

name: Shu Ding
bio: Shu Ding is a designer and developer at Vercel. Public bio covers work on the Vercel platform, Next.js, AI SDK, and v0, after earlier algorithm competitions, web design, Microsoft engineering, and a CS degree from Fudan University. Interests span creative coding, game design, and HCI.
highlights: Vercel: platform, Next.js, AI SDK, v0 craft.
Public site documents creative coding and HCI interests.
Designer-developer bridge for developer tools UX.

name: Steve Schoger
bio: Steve Schoger is a Canadian visual designer known for sharing UI tips publicly and for Refactoring UI, the book and video course made with Adam Wathan. His site describes teaching web design through specific, actionable tactics and refactoring UIs in public. Work centers on practical visual craft rather than theory-only critique.
highlights: Co-author of Refactoring UI with Adam Wathan.
Known for public UI tips and refactor videos.
Site frames design advice for builders shipping interfaces.

name: Tobias van Schneider
bio: Tobias van Schneider is a designer and maker whose public brand centers on independent product and studio craft. His X bio and site point to personal projects including tools and collections aimed at attention and making. Directory entry credits public presence only; no affiliation claimed.
highlights: Independent designer/maker with long public craft presence.
Site and X document products and studio work.
Cited here as a public craft voice—not an endorsement.

name: Yuhki Yamashita
bio: Yuhki Yamashita served as Chief Product Officer at Figma, shaping product direction during a major growth period. Public LinkedIn notes mark the close of a multi-year Figma chapter in 2026. Directory entry credits public product-leadership craft around design tools—not an ongoing role claim beyond published sources.
highlights: Former Chief Product Officer at Figma (public 2026 transition notes).
Associated with expanding what design tools can hold on the canvas.
Listed from public career sources only.

name: Brandon Theriot
bio: Independent study desk of published design principles, prompts, and a public craft directory. Brandon assembles public sources into this browsable site—curator and builder, not an endorsed spokesperson for anyone listed. Personal site link coming; for now GitHub hosts the repos.
highlights: Curates public craft notes into a Quiet Folio reading desk and designer directory.
Status: curator/builder—assembles credits and outbound links, invents nothing unpublished.
Personal page link TBD — placeholder ready.
